verses.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, To those who through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ have received a faith as precious as ours:
Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.

Through these He has given us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.
For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;
and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness;
and to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.
For if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
But whoever lacks these traits is nearsighted to the point of blindness, having forgotten that he has been cleansed from his past sins.
Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure. For if you practice these things you will never stumble,
and you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
Therefore I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
I think it is right to refresh your memory as long as I live in the tent of my body,
because I know that this tent will soon be laid aside, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
And I will make every effort to ensure that after my departure, you will be able to recall these things at all times.
For we did not follow cleverly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.
For He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory, saying, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
And we ourselves heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.

We also have the word of the prophets as confirmed beyond doubt. And you will do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
Above all, you must understand that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one's own interpretation.
For no such prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.

context.author: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ (1:1). Many scholars doubt that Peter wrote it himself, because of its Greek, its use of Jude and how late it appears in the church’s writings; others hold that he wrote it near the end of his life (1:13-15).
context.audience: Believers who have received “a faith as precious as ours” (1:1), probably the churches of the first letter (3:1).
context.mapLabel: ROME, AND THE MOUNT OF TRANSFIGURATION
context.setting: Peter writes as one who knows his death is near. He urges his readers to add virtue, knowledge, self-control, steadfastness, godliness, brotherly affection, and love to their faith. He reminds them that he and the other apostles were eyewitnesses of Christ’s majesty on the holy mountain.
context.custom: Greek writers often listed virtues, and Peter’s list begins with faith and ends with love (1:5-7). Some commentators note that the verb for “add” (1:5) was used of a rich citizen who paid in full for a city’s festival chorus. The “tent” of the body (1:13-14) is a picture Paul also used (2 Corinthians 5:1).
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 2 warns that false teachers will arise, as false prophets did in Israel.
context.timelineBible: The voice from heaven (1:17) is close to the words at Jesus’s baptism and on the mountain (Matthew 3:17; 17:5) and echoes Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1. The star from Jacob (Numbers 24:17) is often linked to the morning star of 1:19. Verses 20-21 say that no prophecy came by human will, but that people spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.
context.sparkNotes: His divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature. Make every effort to supplement your faith with virtue, knowledge, self-control, steadfastness, godliness, brotherly affection, and love. I know that the putting off of my body will be soon. We did not follow cleverly devised myths. We were eyewitnesses of his majesty, and heard the voice on the holy mountain. We have the prophetic word more fully confirmed.

translation.meaning: Sharers, partners. Not becoming God, but sharing in his moral life.
Those who see at first hand, a term used of those initiated in mysteries.

A star shall come out of Jacob.

overview.summary: Peter urges growth in godliness and recalls his eyewitness testimony of the transfiguration, saying that Scripture came from men moved by the Holy Spirit.
overview.settingLine: Peter writes shortly before his death.

history.t: The writer says he will soon lay aside his tent, “as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me” (1:14). John 21:18-19 records what Jesus told Peter about the way he would die, and Clement of Rome says Peter suffered many hardships and went to his place of glory. The letter looks ahead to that departure and promises that the readers will have a reminder after it (1:15).

The letter names Simon Peter (1:1) and claims an eyewitness’s memory of the holy mountain (1:16-18). Origen, Eusebius and Jerome report that some in their day doubted it was Peter’s, and scholars still divide over the author, the date and the readers.

customs.t: Verses 5-7 build a chain of eight links from faith to love. Greek moral writers also listed virtues, but Peter begins with faith and ends with love, and he says God’s power has already supplied everything needed for godliness (1:3). Some commentators compare the verb for “add” to a wealthy citizen who paid in full for a city’s chorus.

Peter calls his body a tent that he will soon put off (1:13-14). A tent was a temporary shelter for a traveler or a soldier, and Paul used the same picture for the body in 2 Corinthians 5:1. Bedouin tents of woven cloth can still be seen in Jordan.

Verse 19 says the prophetic word is like a lamp shining in a dark place until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts. A clay lamp gave only a small light. The morning star, the planet Venus before sunrise, announces the coming day, and Revelation 22:16 gives Jesus the title bright morning star.

archaeology.t: The oldest surviving copy of 2 Peter is in Papyrus 72, a papyrus book from Egypt of the 3rd or 4th century (Papyrus Bodmer VIII, now in the Vatican Library). It copies the two letters of Peter along with Jude and other texts. Eusebius says some doubted 2 Peter, but this book shows it was being read in Egypt by then.

Small clay lamps burned olive oil and gave a dim light. The Getty Museum has one from the 1st century BC to the 4th century AD. It shows the kind of light that a lamp in a dark place gave, which is the picture in 1:19.

Bedouin tents of woven cloth, like this camp at Wadi Rum in Jordan, show what Peter’s picture of the body looked like: a light shelter that can be taken down and moved. Peter says he must soon put off his tent (1:13-14).

overview.discussion: Peter lists a chain of qualities to add to faith. Which link feels weakest in my life right now?
overview.book: The second letter of Peter · 3 chapters. Peter’s last words, written as he expects to die soon.

currentImage.caption: The Church of the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor. Peter says he and the others heard the voice from heaven when they were with Jesus on the holy mountain (1:16-18). He does not name the mountain, and many readers think of Tabor or of Mount Hermon.
